title: How Priyam Raj built micro-SaaS products from India and sold them via creator distribution
summary: Priyam Raj explains how he went from teen blogger to selling a SaaS for 1 crore at 21 and running Vid.ai at about $70k MRR. Core ideas: solve your own problem, validate with content before building, partner with creators for distribution, build an audience as an asset, and treat products as stairs with an exit.

principles.text: Think about marketing before you commit time to building anything.
principles.quote: the first approach should always be you think about marketing before committing any time into the building part right.

principles.text: Start from your own problem, then validate with content and Reddit posts before writing code.
principles.quote: I would start making content about it. I would start positioning tweets about it, maybe res whatever I'm good at, whatever I'm enjoying, right?

principles.text: Partner with a creator whose audience is your moat; it defends against big AI labs and drives revenue.
principles.quote: a really good angle to is uh having a very specific creator under your sleeve like have good relationships with influencers

principles.text: Creator partnerships can launch a product fast: a few videos produced $50k MRR in days.
principles.quote: just through those three four videos we made like 50k MR like $50,000 in uh MR like in just a couple days.

principles.text: Beat bloated incumbents by taking one feature for one segment and making it better.
principles.quote: if you focus on one certain part about an app, there's a good chance you can make it better than even the big cops.

principles.text: Treat products as stairs and plan an exit; selling a bootstrapped business yields capital without raising.
principles.quote: exiting is such a lovely thing in a bootstrap business because you can get a lot of money without raising, right?
